---
title: Themes
description: Choose a theme, install a fixed release, update an older copy, and set light and dark modes.
order: 7
---

A theme is a stylesheet that sets the colours and the fonts of the site. The pages of smalldocs use
[Bootstrap](https://getbootstrap.com), a library of CSS. [Bootswatch](https://bootswatch.com) is a set of
free themes for Bootstrap. smalldocs includes the 25 themes of Bootswatch 5.3, as the CSS files that
Bootswatch builds. To use a
theme, give its name in `theme`, at the top level of `_smalldocs.yml`:

```yaml
theme: flatly
```

In a `_quarto.yml`, `theme` is under `format.html`.

The themes have these names:

- cerulean, cosmo (the default), cyborg, darkly, flatly, journal, litera, lumen, lux
- materia, minty, morph, pulse, quartz, sandstone, simplex, sketchy, slate
- solar, spacelab, superhero, united, vapor, yeti and zephyr

The name `bootstrap` gives Bootstrap with no theme.

## A light theme and a dark theme

If you give two themes, the navbar or the sidebar gets a toggle between them. For example:

```yaml
theme:
  light: cosmo
  dark: darkly
```

On the first visit, the page starts in the mode that the browser prefers. The browser keeps the choice
of the reader after a click on the toggle, and that choice wins on later visits. The page loads the
right theme before it shows anything, so it does not flash the other theme first.

An extension can include both modes under one name. This site uses `theme: folio`, which selects the
light and dark stylesheets of Folio. [The Elegant collection](#themes-in-the-elegant-collection) has
installation examples.

## A theme from a git repository

A theme extension is a theme in a folder of your project, `_extensions/<name>/`. You get it once from a
git repository with `smalldocs add`, and the folder stays in your project. Quarto keeps its extensions
in the same folder.

First, add the theme. Give the repository as `org/repo` on GitHub:

```bash
smalldocs add rahuldave/smalldocs-tufte
```

The command clones the repository with `git clone --depth 1`, over ssh. So it can get a private
repository that your own ssh key can read. It copies each folder of `_extensions/` in the repository
into the `_extensions/` folder of your project, without `.git`. Then it prints the line to use:

```yaml
theme: tufte
```

The source can also be one of these:

- `org/repo@v1.0`: a branch, a tag or a whole commit hash after `@`
- a git URL, such as `git@gitlab.com:org/repo.git` or `https://github.com/org/repo.git`
- a local git repository, or a bare one. smalldocs clones it, so it gets the files of a commit, and not
  the changes that you did not commit
- a local folder with an `_extensions/` folder, which is not a git repository. smalldocs copies its
  files as they are

If the folder of an extension is already in your project, the command asks before it replaces the
folder. Give `--force` to replace it without a question.

`theme` takes the name of the folder. The name works alone, or with a Bootswatch theme:

```yaml
theme: tufte              # the light and the dark CSS of the extension, and a toggle
theme:
  light: tufte            # the light CSS of the extension
  dark: darkly            # a Bootswatch theme
```

smalldocs also looks in `_extensions/<org>/<name>/`, the other folder layout of Quarto. If two folders
have the same name, or an extension has the name of a Bootswatch theme, the build stops with an error.
If no theme has the name, the error lists the names you can use.

In a `_quarto.yml`, a theme extension for both tools is often a custom format of Quarto. Give its name
with `-html` in `format`:

```yaml
format:
  tufte-html:
    toc: true
```

Quarto uses the format of the extension. smalldocs reads the options under `tufte-html` as the options
under `html`. If `_extensions/tufte/` has a `smalldocs.yml`, smalldocs also uses its theme.

You can also write the theme of smalldocs under `smalldocs:`. Quarto reads `format.html.theme`, and
smalldocs reads `smalldocs.theme`, so each tool gets its own theme:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, _extensions/tufte/tufte.scss]
smalldocs:
  theme: tufte
```

### What the build copies

The build copies the CSS of the theme into `_site/site_libs/themes/<name>/`. It also copies each file
that the CSS uses through `url(...)` or `@import`, such as a font or an image. A file outside the folder
of the extension is not copied, and the build gives a warning. The build does not copy the other files
of the extension, and it never copies `_extensions/` itself into the site.

If your site sets no logo, the site uses the logo of the theme. If it sets no favicon, the site uses
the favicon of the theme. A favicon is the small picture in the tab of the browser.

### See what is installed

`smalldocs add` writes a file `.source` in the folder of each extension. The file holds the source as
you gave it, the ref after `@`, and the commit that git cloned:

```yaml
source: rahuldave/smalldocs-tufte@v0.1.0
ref: v0.1.0
commit: 5f0c2a9e...
```

`smalldocs themes` lists the bundled themes, and each extension of the project with its source:

```bash
smalldocs themes
```

### Update a theme

Run `smalldocs add` again with `--force`. To get the newest commit of the default branch, leave out the
ref:

```bash
smalldocs add rahuldave/smalldocs-tufte --force
```

To get a release, give its tag, such as `@v0.2.0`. `smalldocs themes` prints the command that gets
the same source again, and the command that gets the newest commit. Commit the folder `_extensions/` with your project, so that each build uses the
same theme.

## Themes in the Elegant collection

The [Elegant collection](https://rahuldave.com/elegant-themes/) compares themes on the same pages.
It includes the original custom designs and their refinements, with source links and example sites.

The [theme handbook](https://rahuldave.com/elegant-themes/theme-guide.html) describes each theme,
its fonts and its colour modes. It also shows how to add optional labels above page titles.

Folio, Atelier and Nocturne include light and dark modes. Their revised release is `v0.2.0`.
The Reading themes are separate extensions that keep the native palette of a Bootswatch theme.
The current default branches omit the fixed title labels. The pinned `v0.2.0` release still includes them.

| Theme and example | Name in `theme:` | Modes |
|---|---|---|
| [Folio](https://rahuldave.com/smalldocs-folio/) | [`folio`](https://github.com/rahuldave/smalldocs-folio) | Light and dark |
| [Atelier](https://rahuldave.com/smalldocs-atelier/) | [`atelier`](https://github.com/rahuldave/smalldocs-atelier) | Light and dark |
| [Nocturne](https://rahuldave.com/smalldocs-nocturne/) | [`nocturne`](https://github.com/rahuldave/smalldocs-nocturne) | Light and dark |
| [Zephyr Reading](https://rahuldave.com/smalldocs-zephyr-reading/) | [`zephyr-reading`](https://github.com/rahuldave/smalldocs-zephyr-reading) | Light |
| [Simplex Reading](https://rahuldave.com/smalldocs-simplex-reading/) | [`simplex-reading`](https://github.com/rahuldave/smalldocs-simplex-reading) | Light |
| [Pulse Reading](https://rahuldave.com/smalldocs-pulse-reading/) | [`pulse-reading`](https://github.com/rahuldave/smalldocs-pulse-reading) | Light |
| [Litera Reading](https://rahuldave.com/smalldocs-litera-reading/) | [`litera-reading`](https://github.com/rahuldave/smalldocs-litera-reading) | Light |
| [Darkly Reading](https://rahuldave.com/smalldocs-darkly-reading/) | [`darkly-reading`](https://github.com/rahuldave/smalldocs-darkly-reading) | Dark |

The name links to the source repository. The install source is `rahuldave/smalldocs-` followed by the
name, as in the commands below.

### Install Folio

Run the command in the folder with your `_smalldocs.yml`:

```bash
smalldocs add rahuldave/smalldocs-folio
```

Set the theme, then render the site:

```yaml
theme: folio
```

```bash
smalldocs render
```

The command gets the newest commit of the default branch, including the title label cleanup.
Add a tag to select a fixed release. The extension includes compiled CSS and local fonts, so installation needs no Sass compiler.

### Update the original Atelier

The revised Atelier keeps the name `atelier`. Existing sites keep their installed copy until you
replace it. To install the current theme without the fixed title label:

```bash
smalldocs add rahuldave/smalldocs-atelier --force
smalldocs render
```

Keep `theme: atelier`. The command replaces `_extensions/atelier/`. Keep any local theme changes in
your own stylesheet before replacing that folder. Commit the updated extension with your project.

Use `smalldocs themes` to see the installed source and commit. Folio and Nocturne use the same update
commands, with their own repository names.

The original custom designs remain at the tag `before-reading-redesign-2026-10-16`.
To restore the original Atelier:

```bash
smalldocs add rahuldave/smalldocs-atelier@before-reading-redesign-2026-10-16 --force
smalldocs render
```

The configuration name stays `atelier` for both versions.

### Use a Reading theme

The Reading extensions have separate names from the bundled themes. For example, `litera` selects the
stock Bootswatch theme and `litera-reading` selects the refinement. Install the refinement first:

```bash
smalldocs add rahuldave/smalldocs-litera-reading
```

```yaml
theme: litera-reading
```

You can pair a light Reading theme with Darkly Reading. Install both extensions:

```bash
smalldocs add rahuldave/smalldocs-litera-reading
smalldocs add rahuldave/smalldocs-darkly-reading
```

```yaml
theme:
  light: litera-reading
  dark: darkly-reading
```

The navbar or sidebar shows the mode toggle. A Reading extension has one native palette; Folio,
Atelier and Nocturne have both modes in one extension.

### Read the assessments and principles

The collection has separate assessments for typography and visual design. Each scores themes out of
100, with the same criteria before and after refinement. The scores come from a self-review of shared
specimens.

- [Typography assessment](https://rahuldave.com/elegant-themes/typography-report.html)
- [Visual design assessment](https://rahuldave.com/elegant-themes/visual-design-report.html)
- [Typography principles](https://rahuldave.com/elegant-themes/typography-guide.html)
- [UI design principles](https://rahuldave.com/elegant-themes/ui-design-guide.html)

The typography criteria draw on [Butterick's Practical Typography](https://practicaltypography.com/).
The visual design criteria draw on [Refactoring UI](https://refactoringui.com/).

## Make a theme for smalldocs and Quarto

One repository can hold a theme for both tools. Each tool reads its own files in the same folder, and
ignores the files of the other tool:

```
_extensions/tufte/
  _extension.yml     # Quarto reads this
  tufte.scss         # Quarto compiles this Sass
  smalldocs.yml      # smalldocs reads this
  tufte.css          # the light theme for smalldocs: all of Bootstrap 5.3, then your rules
  tufte-dark.css     # the dark theme for smalldocs
  et-book/           # fonts, which both CSS files use through url(...)
  logo.svg
```

`smalldocs.yml` names the files:

```yaml
css:
  light: tufte.css
  dark: tufte-dark.css
logo: logo.svg       # optional. The site uses it only when it sets no logo
favicon: logo.svg    # optional. The site uses it only when it sets no favicon
```

`css` can also name one file, which smalldocs uses as a light theme. A file in `smalldocs.yml` must be
inside the folder of the extension.

smalldocs compiles no Sass. So each CSS file is a complete Bootstrap 5.3 stylesheet, as a Bootswatch
file is. Make it from `tufte.scss` with a Sass compiler. Or put the CSS of Bootstrap first, and your
own rules after it.

The stylesheet of smalldocs loads after the theme. If a rule of your theme sets the same property on the
same element as a rule of smalldocs, the rule of smalldocs wins. Start such a rule with `html`, as in
`html h2`, so that it wins. The next section tells you which variables to set.

## How the page gets the colours of the theme

Bootswatch writes each theme in Sass, a language that a compiler turns into CSS. smalldocs uses the CSS
that Bootswatch builds, so it needs no Sass compiler. A Bootstrap 5.3 theme sets its colours, fonts and
borders as CSS variables, such as `--bs-primary`, `--bs-body-bg` and `--bs-border-color`.

The stylesheet of smalldocs lays out the navbar, the sidebar, the table of contents, the callouts and
the listings. It uses only those variables. So each part of the page gets the colours of the theme,
in the light theme and in the dark theme.

## Fonts and colours from options

These options of a page change the fonts, the colours and the width of the theme. Set them at the top
level of `_smalldocs.yml`, in a `_metadata.yml` file, or in front matter:

```yaml
mainfont: "Georgia, serif"   # the font of the text
monofont: "Menlo, monospace" # the font of code
fontsize: 16px               # the size of 1rem; 17px if you set none
linestretch: 1.6             # the height of a line of text
linkcolor: "#1a5fb4"         # the colour of links
backgroundcolor: "#fdfdf8"   # the colour of the page
fontcolor: "#222222"         # the colour of the text
max-width: 900px             # the width of the text; 760px if you set none
```

smalldocs writes each value into a CSS variable of Bootstrap or of smalldocs, after its own stylesheet
and before your `css`. Write `linkcolor`, `backgroundcolor` and `fontcolor` as a hex colour such as
`#1a5fb4`, or as `rgb()`. Bootstrap needs the red, green and blue parts of the colour of links. The
build leaves out a value with `<`, `>`, `{`, `}`, `;` or a backslash, and gives a warning.

The colours apply to the light theme and to the dark theme. With two themes, set the colours in your
own CSS instead, under `html.quarto-dark` for the dark theme.

## Your own CSS

```yaml
theme: cosmo
css: styles.css
```

The browser loads `styles.css` after the theme and after the stylesheet of smalldocs. In it, set the
variables of Bootstrap to change the theme, or the variables of smalldocs to change the layout:

```css
:root {
  --bs-primary: #7a3e9d;     /* the colours of Bootstrap */
  --sd-body-width: 900px;    /* the width of the text */
  --sd-sidebar-width: 280px; /* the width of the sidebar */
  --sd-root-font-size: 16px; /* the size of 1rem, which sets every size of text; 17px if you set none */
}
```

smalldocs does not compile a `.scss` file in `theme`. The build gives a warning about it.

If the name of your CSS file ends in `.min.css`, the site keeps that name. A file `my.css` becomes
`my.min.css` in `site_libs/themes/`.
